stage_a.note: Founder speaks with a warm smile, open gestures, and clear enthusiasm about his wine.
Sustained engagement and excitement as he describes the revolutionary packaging and stadium potential.
He is friendly and approachable, smiling while he toasts the panel, but mostly professional.

venture.description: A premium wine packaged in a single-serve, ready-to-drink glass designed for stadiums, events, and retail.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder introduces Copa Di Vino, a premium wine by the glass, seeking investment to expand inventory for retailers and stadiums.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks if the founder is selling a packaging system or entering the competitive wine business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder confirms he has a winery, producing cases annually, and has sold into numerous states through large distributors.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder hands out samples of the packaged wine to the investors.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark asks if the founder grows his own grapes for the wine.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder clarifies that he buys fruit from friends who own vineyards.

turns.speaker: PANEL
turns.summary: The panel and founder toast and taste the wine samples.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder asks if it was the easiest glass of wine they have ever served themselves.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert notes that the seal is a little hard to take off.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks whether he would be buying into a wine label or a packaging system.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder explains there are three revenue streams: licensing, industry bottling, and their own consumer brand.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks which of the three revenue streams are currently bringing in sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder states that their own consumer brand is currently generating the sales.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks what the current sales figures are for the consumer brand.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder shares they have half a million in sales and significant pending orders in five months.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara expresses positive surprise at the quick sales growth.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert seeks to confirm that customers buy the wine primarily because it is easy to carry.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder agrees but adds that customers are also getting a good quality product.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin argues the product is not premium wine but rather industrial wine.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara teases Kevin, calling him a wine snob.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin reiterates he wouldn't buy the wine, asserting the true value is in the mass-market packaging play.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond asks how long the wine stays fresh while sitting on a shelf.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder explains the packaging extends the typically short shelf life of small amounts to a full year.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks if the founder has patented the packaging system.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder confirms the patent, describing the atmospheric packaging technology developed with top laboratories.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond asks where the product is currently being sold.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder lists major retail chains they are selling to or in discussions with.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks why they don't just license the packaging to major wineries instead of being in the wine business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder states they are already working on projects with two of the largest global wine companies.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks how much money the founder expects to make from those licensing deals.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder estimates three to five million dollars in sales for the following year.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks why they aren't marketing the patent asset directly to large packaging companies instead of bottling.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder explains the wine industry needs proof of concept and prefers to outsource this specialized packaging process.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond states the venture is too early for him and exits the deal.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks if it is possible to separate the patent from the rest of the business.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin also asks if they can pull the licensing IP apart from the wine company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder agrees they can be separated and invites the investors to propose a valuation and structure.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder attempts to pivot the conversation to Mark's stadium attendance.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark acknowledges he could be a customer but states he does not want to be in commission sales.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks how much of the IP company and bottler he could own for the requested investment amount.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder offers the original twenty percent equity stake.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin immediately states that twenty percent is not enough equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder argues that Kevin has already devalued the brand portion to zero.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert explains he doesn't want to build a wine brand or split the company, so he exits.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara states she cannot bring any additional value to the table and exits.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asserts that the real value and business opportunity lies entirely in the packaging IP.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder briefly acknowledges Kevin's point.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin presses the founder to focus on selling the IP and asks how much he can buy for the requested amount.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder states he is not ready to give away his competitive advantages to another entity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder elaborates that the financial opportunity lies more in the bottling side than just the IP.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert briefly acknowledges the founder's point.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin offers for a majority stake in just the IP, planning to license it while the founder runs the brand.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder argues the overall opportunity is much greater than Kevin's offer suggests.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark states Kevin's deal is better than what he would offer and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder attempts to further explain his vision and the value of keeping the business integrated.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert advises the founder to stop selling since he already has an offer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin jokes that he is a dream come true for the founder.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder defends keeping the special sauce integrated, citing significant personal investment and large pending contracts.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond jokingly asks if Kevin will ever get a direct answer to his offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder explicitly rejects Kevin's offer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks the founder to counter his offer for the majority stake.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder counters with a significantly higher valuation for the requested equity.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin withdraws his offer and exits, criticizing the founder for walking away from the opportunity.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark comments critically on the founder's handling of the negotiation.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin agrees with Mark's critical assessment.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder toasts the panel and thanks them before leaving.

decisions.note: Too early for him; pioneers get slaughtered.
Does not want to build a wine brand or split the company.
Feels she cannot bring anything to the table.
Wants majority control of the IP to license it, leaving the brand to the founder.
Believes Kevin's deal is far better than anything he would offer.
Refuses to give up control of the special sauce.
Significantly increases the valuation for the requested equity.
Rejects the counter and criticizes the founder for losing the opportunity.

record.notes: The pitch includes an extended negotiation about separating the IP from the wine brand.
